Resolve a comparison into one carried answer

Source: R/policy.R
quorum_resolve.Rd

Walks the policy's declared order and carries the first lens that is present, grounded and decisive for that cell. When no lens is, but at least one is present and grounded and simply would not stand behind a number, the policy's status_quo is carried and the cell is recorded as having defaulted. When nothing grounded remains, the cell abstains and carries no number at all.

Usage

quorum_resolve(contrib, policy)

Arguments

contrib

A contributions data frame from contributions(). A cell column makes the resolution per cell; without one the whole table is treated as a single cell.

policy

A quorum_policy() or a policy_committed().

Value

A data frame with one row per cell: cell (when the input had one), a tier_<lens> logical for each lens in the policy's order, tier_status_quo, tier_abstain, carried_lens, verdict ("decide", "default" or "abstain") and action.

Details

The three outcomes are deliberately distinct. A defaulting cell has a grounded lens that declined; an abstaining cell has none, and the difference is the whole reason an abstention is not simply resolved to a fixed rate. A lens that abstained never contributes its number to either.

Handed a policy_committed(), the function applies that convention instead of the cascade and returns the same columns, so the two are comparable cell by cell.

Only lenses named in policy@order take part: a contribution from a lens the policy did not declare is carried in the table but not in the resolution.

See also

contributions(), quorum_compare_policies(), quorum().

Examples

contrib <- contributions(
  lens_contribution("mechanism", grounded = TRUE, abstained = TRUE),
  lens_contribution("statistical", grounded = TRUE, abstained = FALSE,
                    action = 30)
)
quorum_resolve(contrib, quorum_policy(c("mechanism", "statistical"),
                                      status_quo = 60))
#>   tier_mechanism tier_statistical tier_status_quo tier_abstain carried_lens
#> 1          FALSE             TRUE           FALSE        FALSE  statistical
#>   verdict action
#> 1  decide     30
